The two labels look statistically independent in the data, so there is no sign of a causal link in either direction.

- Among patients without L C6 radiculopathy, 1,379 of 12,064 (11.4%) have R tibia pain.
- Among patients with L C6 radiculopathy, 487 of 4,320 (11.3%) have R tibia pain.

The rate of R tibia pain is essentially the same whether or not L C6 radiculopathy is present. I did not run a formal test. The near-identical rates, and a left cervical root and a right tibia that are anatomically unrelated, point to C.

ANSWER: C
